# E0348: binding named like a value parameter

A type written after this binding would still mean the value parameter, not the binding. Give the binding another name.

- Rule: [`generics.value-parameters-in-body`](../../reference/07-types.md#generics.value-parameters-in-body)
- Reported at: the binding's name.
- Tier: `meta`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0348:4
use std.array

fn last<n: i64>(a: array.Array<i64, n>) -> i64 {
  let n = n - 1
  a[n]
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
use std.array

fn last<n: i64>(a: array.Array<i64, n>) -> i64 {
  let i = n - 1
  a[i]
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0348_binding_named_like_a_value_parameter.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0348_binding_named_like_a_value_parameter.lt):

```text
── BINDING NAMED LIKE A VALUE PARAMETER ── E0348_binding_named_like_a_value_parameter.lt:4:7  [E0348]

`n` is a value parameter here, and a type written after this binding would still
name the parameter, so no binding takes its name: rename this one:

  4 │   let n = n - 1
    │       ^

A type written after this binding would still mean the value parameter, not the
binding. Give the binding another name.
```
